newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco garbage collectors go on strike.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco garbage collectors go on strike.

text.p: Garbage bags started to pile up on sidewalks Thursday after hundreds of San Francisco trash collectors went on strike to back demands for higher wages and improved health benefits.

Union leaders called the strike at midnight after workers rejected the latest contract offer by Sunset Scavenger Co. and Golden Gate Disposal & Recycling Co., subsidiaries of Norcal Waste Systems Inc. which collect San Francisco's garbage.
News reports said the strike involved about 600 garbage collectors who have worked without a contract since Dec. 31. It was San Francisco's first garbage collectors' strike in 57 years.
The strike would affect every home and business in San Francisco, union leaders said. Garbage bags lay uncollected in some neighbourhoods Thursday.

"We feel sorry for the citizens because they're the ones who will suffer due to the lack of service in restaurants, hotels, hospitals," said Robert Morales, a spokesman for the Sanitary Truck Drivers and Helpers Local 350.
Union officials said workers would stay off the job for as long as necessary. But Morales said they were ready to resume negotiations "as soon as we get a call from management."

San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown and the director of the city's public works department met Thursday to discuss how to deal with the strike. City officials told reporters after the meeting that they would not intervene for now.

Workers are seeking a three-year contract, an 80-cents-per-hour pay increase, an early retirement plan and improved health benefits. The average garbage truck driver now earns $20.58 per hour or $49,000 a year.

The companies offered two alternatives, one of which would boost pay 19.3 percent over five years. The other package would have provided more modest wage increases but more funds for health care and pension benefits.
The last time San Francisco garbage collectors went on strike was 1940. It lasted two days.
